gap: No result ChatGPT got states how long a full four-cell load of 18650s takes on each charger. The pages it got give per-slot amps, or a single-cell time, or a four-cell time for one charger only. Our arithmetic floor for four 3,000 mAh cells: about 1 h on a Vapcell S4 Plus V3 (3 A × 4), 3 h on an XTAR VC4SL or VX4 (1 A × 4), and 12 h on a Tenergy TN270 (0.5 A × 2 bays, two loads).
standout_why: Compared against 1lumen.com VC4SL (cited), m0mnf.com (cited), timmcmahon.com.au VX4 (cited), xtar.cc comparison, beamandbattery.com and besttacticalflashlighttoday.net. 1Lumen and M0MNF give the VC4SL's 3A×1/2A×2/1A×4 split and a single-cell time of 1.2 h (3,000 mAh at 3,060 mA) but no four-cell time. Tim McMahon lists the VX4's 1Ax4 spec and only tested one channel. xtar.cc gives only the maximum current, 3 A, with no split by number of loaded slots. Beam & Battery has no all-bay currents or times. Besttacticalflashlighttoday has part of it: about 3.5 h for four 3,000 mAh cells on the Nitecore UMS4 and 1 A each for four on the VC4SL. It has no figure for the Vapcell or the Tenergy, and nothing that compares the four-slot rate across chargers. ChatGPT's own answer says the S4 Plus does 'up to 3A per slot simultaneously' but never turns that into time saved.
decides: This confirms the split ChatGPT hinted at, now as hours. ChatGPT's 'best overall' picks (VC4SL, VX4) drop to 1 A per slot when all four bays are full, so a full load takes 3 h or more. The Vapcell S4 Plus V3 is rated to keep 3 A in every bay, about 1 h, so it's the pick for anyone who regularly charges four cells at once. The VC4SL/VX4 stay the value picks for one or two cells, where they reach 3 A or 2 A. Dealectric's own listed Tenergy TN270 (0.5 A, 2 bays) needs about 12 h of constant-current time for four cells, so the page shouldn't pitch it as a fast 18650 pick.

findings.label: Li-ion charge current per slot by number of cells loaded
findings.value: 3 A with 1 cell, 2 A each with 2, 1 A each with 4
findings.note: 1Lumen: 'if you put in 2 cells then it will charge them at up to 2A each (4A total) and 4 at a time only goes up to 1A'. Full speed needs a QC USB-C source of about 18 W. M0MNF (m0mnf.com/reviews/battcharge.php) states the same 4×1 A / 2×2 A / 1×3 A split.

findings.label: Measured single-cell charge time, 3,000 mAh 18650 at 3 A
findings.note: 1Lumen table: 18650 (3000 mAh), 3,060 mA, 1.2 h, ended at 4.19 V. The constant-current floor is 3.0 Ah ÷ 3.06 A = 0.98 h, so the constant-voltage tail added about 0.2 h (about 20%) in this test. The review doesn't say how many bays were loaded.

findings.label: Derived: constant-current time to charge four 3,000 mAh 18650s at once
findings.note: 3.0 Ah ÷ 1 A per slot (4 loaded) = 3.0 h. Power check: 4 × 4.2 V × 1 A = 16.8 W, inside the roughly 18 W QC input 1Lumen gives. Besttacticalflashlighttoday gives about 3.5 h for four 3,000 mAh cells at 1 A on a similar 4-bay charger, which fits floor plus tail.

The manuals.plus V3 manual that ChatGPT cited returned 403 to me, so check this against the manual before publishing. akkuteile: 'Total power 12A / 3A per charging slot'. It doesn't name the version, so V3 is assumed. The Makiuto review (makiuto.github.io, 23 Dec 2025, no named author) repeats the product claim 'Three Amp Charge Rate Available on All Bays at One Time'; it is a claim, not a measurement. Power check: 4 × 4.2 V × 3 A = 50.4 W, under a 12 V × 5 A = 60 W supply, so the claim is electrically plausible.
